newsitem.title: MEXICO: GMexico sees rail bid as separate business venture.
newsitem.headline: GMexico sees rail bid as separate business venture.

text.p: Grupo Mexico, known as GMexico, considers its bidding for rights to operate the Pacific-North railway as a separate business venture, Deputy Finance Director Carlos Oyanguren said Monday.

In an interview, Oyanguren said that although the rail network had some synergies with GMexico's core mining and metals business it would be treated apart if GMexico's consortium wins the 50-year operating rights.

"In the event we win the concession, there is going to be no advantage. GMexico will pay the same (freight) costs as any other user," Oyanguren said. "We see it as a totally separate business," he added.

GMexico has submitted a sealed bid for an 80 percent stake in the Pacific-North network. The bid is backed by Union Pacific and construction giant Empresas ICA under the consortium Grupo Ferroviario Mexicano (GFM).
GFM is 74 percent controlled by GMexico and 13 percent each of the other partners.

Mexico is privatising its railroads in chunks in a bid to modernise the train system and create a viable transportation alternative to roads. The government will keep a 20 percent stake in the network.
The government is considering GFM's technical proposals this week and will open the consortium's financial proposals on June 26.
GFM will be awarded the operating concession if the amount tendered is above the government's floor price for Pacific North. That floor price has not been divulged and is also in a sealed envelope.

Analysts had suggested one of the reasons why GMexico wanted to move into the railroad business was to link synergies with the companies mine and metals complexes in the north of Mexico as a cost cutting measure.
